title: Only 15% Of Adults Can Pass This Dentist Entrance Exam
summary: Explore dental knowledge through clues, practical situations and fresh challenges.

landing.intro:
Know the science behind a smile?
Test what lies beneath.

about.body: Connect the facts, notice the details and test your understanding of dental knowledge. Each checkpoint reveals your topic profile before a different challenge begins.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not a real dental-school entrance examination, professional qualification or source of personal dental advice.

next.tagline: Up next: Plaque and gum health.
Up next: Tooth surfaces and bite.
Up next: Dental tools and images.

dentist-s1q1.question: Which teeth are shaped mainly for cutting food?

dentist-s1q2.question: Which teeth have pointed crowns suited to tearing food?

dentist-s1q3.question: Which teeth have broad chewing surfaces for grinding?

answers.a3: All teeth have a single sharp point

dentist-s1q4.question: How many teeth are in a complete primary dentition?

dentist-s1q5.question: How many teeth are in a complete adult dentition including all third molars?

dentist-s1q6.question: What is another name for third molars?

answers.a1: Primary and permanent teeth are both present

dentist-s2q1.question: What covers the visible crown of a healthy tooth?

dentist-s2q3.question: What is inside the dental pulp?

dentist-s2q4.question: What normally covers the root surface?

dentist-s2q5.question: What helps attach a tooth to the surrounding socket?

dentist-s2q7.question: What is the alveolar bone’s role around teeth?

dentist-s3q1.question: What helps lubricate food and begin digestion in the mouth?

dentist-s3q2.question: Which enzyme in saliva begins starch digestion?

answers.a2: The bony front portion of the roof of the mouth
answers.a4: The lower border of the jaw

dentist-s3q4.question: Which bone forms the lower jaw?

dentist-s3q5.question: Which bones form the upper jaw?

dentist-s3q6.question: Which muscle is strongly involved in closing the jaw?

dentist-s3q7.question: What does the temporomandibular joint connect?

answers.a3: The mandible with the temporal bone of the skull

answers.a1: A biofilm of microorganisms on tooth surfaces
answers.a2: The inside of a salivary gland

dentist-s4q2.question: How can plaque bacteria contribute to tooth decay?

answers.a1: They produce acids from fermentable carbohydrates
answers.a4: They remove every nutrient from blood

answers.a1: Loss of all tooth enamel at birth

answers.a2: A different number of salivary glands
answers.a3: Damage to the tissues supporting the teeth
answers.a4: The presence of any permanent tooth

dentist-s4q6.question: Why is dry mouth relevant to oral health?

answers.a1: Dry mouth always proves one specific disease
answers.a2: Teeth need no moisture at any time
answers.a3: Saliva helps protect and clean the mouth

dentist-s4q7.question: What is the purpose of cleaning between teeth?

answers.a1: To change permanent teeth into primary teeth
answers.a2: To remove plaque and debris from spaces a brush may miss
answers.a3: To shorten the roots of healthy teeth

dentist-s5q1.question: On a tooth, what does the occlusal surface refer to?

answers.a2: The chewing surface of a back tooth

dentist-s5q2.question: What does buccal mean when describing a tooth surface?

dentist-s5q3.question: What does lingual mean when describing a tooth surface?

dentist-s5q4.question: What does a mesial tooth surface face?

answers.a1: Toward the midline of the dental arch
answers.a4: Away from the midline of the dental arch

answers.a3: How the upper and lower teeth meet

answers.a1: A tooth with a newly polished surface
answers.a2: A tooth prevented from erupting normally

dentist-s5q7.question: What is the apex of a tooth root?

answers.a3: The centre of the upper lip

dentist-s6q1.question: Hands are visibly dirty. Which cleaning method is appropriate?

answers.a3: Put gloves on over the dirt

dentist-s6q2.question: What should happen after protective gloves are removed?

answers.a2: Clean hands only if a glove tore
answers.a4: Keep the gloves for another person

dentist-s6q3.question: Which container is designed for used needles and other sharps?

answers.a2: An open tray for later sorting

dentist-s6q4.question: A task may splash body fluid toward the face. Which protection addresses that risk?

dentist-s6q5.question: Shared observation equipment has been used. What should happen before reuse?

answers.a1: Use it unchanged if it looks shiny
answers.a2: Cover old marks with a label
answers.a3: Clean it using the approved method

dentist-s6q6.question: A sterile package is torn before use. What is the safe conclusion?

answers.a1: The contents are sterile if they look clean
answers.a4: The printed date cancels the tear

dentist-s6q7.question: Which statement about protective gloves is correct?

answers.a1: They stay clean regardless of what they touch
answers.a2: The same pair is suitable for every patient
answers.a4: They do not replace hand hygiene

dentist-s7q1.question: What does a dental mirror help the clinician do?

answers.a1: View areas that are difficult to see directly

dentist-s7q2.question: What is a dental radiograph used to visualise?

answers.a3: Teeth and surrounding structures using X-rays
answers.a4: Only the colour of the tongue

dentist-s7q3.question: What does a periodontal probe help measure?

answers.a3: The depth of the space between tooth and gum
answers.a4: The length of the entire arm

dentist-s7q4.question: What is the purpose of dental suction?

answers.a4: Remove saliva and fluid from the working area

dentist-s7q5.question: What is a dental impression or digital scan used to capture?

answers.a1: The shape of teeth and oral structures
answers.a2: The exact age of every tooth
answers.a4: The electrical rhythm of the heart

dentist-s7q6.question: What does a dental restoration aim to do?

answers.a4: Repair damaged or missing tooth structure

dentist-s7q7.question: What does a dental crown cover?

answers.a1: Only the back of the throat
answers.a2: Only the inside of a blood vessel
answers.a4: The prepared or damaged crown portion of a tooth

dentist-s8q1.question: A person says, “I’m worried about what happens next.” What is the best opening?

answers.a2: Promise there is no possible risk
answers.a3: Acknowledge the worry and invite questions

dentist-s8q2.question: Someone wants to discuss a sensitive concern in a busy public area. What protects privacy?

answers.a1: Write the details on a public board

dentist-s8q3.question: A person has not understood an explanation. What helps check understanding?

answers.a1: Explain plainly and ask them to describe it in their own words
answers.a2: Treat a nod as proof of understanding
answers.a4: Ask another patient to answer for them

dentist-s8q4.question: Before a non-urgent examination, what should the person receive?

answers.a1: Only a form with no explanation
answers.a2: A decision made by the nearest visitor
answers.a3: An assurance that questions are not allowed
answers.a4: A clear explanation and an opportunity to consent

dentist-s8q5.question: A person declines having students present. What is the respectful response?

answers.a2: Assume silence later cancels the choice
answers.a4: Respect the choice and protect privacy

dentist-s8q6.question: A language barrier makes an important discussion difficult. What is the best support?

answers.a1: Asking a young child to interpret sensitive details

dentist-s8q7.question: A person with hearing difficulty asks you to repeat yourself. What is helpful?

answers.a3: Face them and check their preferred way to communicate

dentist-s9q1.question: A record shows 850 mL plus 250 mL. What is the total?

dentist-s9q2.question: How many millilitres are in 1.5 L?

dentist-s9q3.question: How much time passes from 09:20 to 10:05?

dentist-s9q4.question: You count 9 breaths in 30 seconds. What is the equivalent rate per minute?

dentist-s9q5.question: A recorded total rises from 600 mL to 900 mL. What is the percentage increase?

dentist-s9q6.question: Divide 1.2 L equally across four recorded periods. How much belongs to each?

dentist-s9q7.question: Three sealed boxes hold eight items each. How many items are there?

dentist-s10q1.question: A tooth is sensitive, but the cause has not been assessed. What is the sound conclusion?

answers.a1: Sensitivity always proves a cracked jaw
answers.a2: Several causes are possible and assessment is needed

dentist-s10q2.question: Why distinguish pain reported by a patient from findings on examination?

answers.a1: Only reported pain can ever matter
answers.a2: Both must always use identical words
answers.a4: They provide different kinds of information

dentist-s10q3.question: A dental record names the left side, but a referral names the right. What needs clarification?

answers.a2: Nothing if the handwriting is clear

dentist-s10q4.question: A child has both primary and permanent teeth. What should a chart distinguish?

answers.a2: Which teeth belong to each dentition
answers.a4: Only the size of the toothbrush

dentist-s10q5.question: Why ask about relevant medicines and allergies before dental treatment?

answers.a1: They make a dental history unnecessary
answers.a2: They prove no examination is needed
answers.a3: They determine the colour of every tooth

dentist-s10q6.question: A patient does not understand a proposed procedure. What is the best next step?

answers.a1: Explain it clearly and invite questions before seeking consent
answers.a2: Treat a blank form as understanding

dentist-s10q7.question: A record has no entry about gum bleeding. What can be concluded from the missing entry alone?
